title: Wrong options stated as claims
statement: Write each wrong option as a plain claim stated as if true, not as a report of what learners believe.
example: Options carried over in the voice 'Some students may believe that...' passed 1 of 5.
detail: A five-item pilot drew wrong options from a bank of misconceptions written in a teaching voice ("Some students may believe that..."), and its instruction to preserve meaning carried that voice into the options. It passed 1/5, at about $0.003. The fix was one line in the prompt: strip the teaching frame and state the wrong belief as if a confused student were asserting it as fact.
against: none found (the re-run after the one-line fix was not in the files read)

evidence.quote: The source corpus (`common_misconceptions`) is written in **pedagogical-meta voice**: "Some students may believe that..." The prompt instructed "preserve semantics," which faithfully carried that voice into MCQ distractor text.
But a real distractor must be a **positive declarative claim** (first-person voice of the wrong belief).
**Fix:** One line in prompt — "Strip any meta-pedagogical framing. The option states the wrong belief AS IF a confused student were asserting it as fact."
